desc:
A social media brand guidelines document is a short written rulebook for how your brand looks, sounds and replies online. Ecom Swift LLC writes it in plain language, so anyone who posts for you can keep every post consistent.

## What is a social media brand guidelines document?

A social media brand guidelines document is a short guide that tells everyone who posts for a business how the brand should look, sound and behave on each channel. It covers colors, fonts, photo style, tone of voice, wording rules and how to handle comments. It is written for people who post, not for designers, so it stays practical.

## Why brands drift when several people post

When one founder writes every caption, the voice stays steady almost by accident. The moment a freelancer, a cousin, an assistant or a part-time employee starts posting, small differences appear. One person writes formal captions, another uses slang, a third adds a different shade of blue to every graphic. Followers may not name the problem, but the feed starts to look like several businesses sharing one account.

Drift also shows up in replies. A complaint answered kindly on Monday and defensively on Friday teaches customers that the brand is unpredictable. Written rules remove that guesswork and make a handover far easier when someone leaves.

## How written rules improve your results

Consistency helps people recognize you. When your colors, photo style and phrasing repeat, a shopper scrolling quickly can tell a post is yours before reading the name. Recognition builds familiarity, and familiarity makes people more willing to click, follow and buy.

Guidelines also save time and cost. Posters make fewer wrong guesses, approvals take fewer rounds, and new helpers become useful faster. The guide does not promise more followers or sales by itself. It removes avoidable mistakes so the effort you already spend on content works harder.

## What a strong guide includes

- Logo rules: clear space, approved versions and what never to do to it.
- Your brand colors and fonts, with where each one is used.
- Photo and graphic style, with plain examples of on-brand and off-brand images.
- Tone of voice in a few points, each backed by a sample sentence.
- A short list of words and phrases to use, and a list to avoid.
- Rules for emojis, hashtags and capital letters.
- Reply rules for common questions, praise and complaints.
- Topics you never post about, and who to ask when unsure.
- Approval steps: who drafts, who checks, who publishes.
- Do and don't examples that a new person can copy within minutes.

## What we do

We start with a short brief and a look at your current profiles, your website and a few of your best posts. We pick out what already feels like you and what is inconsistent. Then we write the guide in simple language, with real examples drawn from your products and audience.

The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ mainly in depth. The smaller guide covers the essentials of look and voice. The middle one adds sample captions and reply rules. The fullest version adds approval steps, hashtag and emoji rules, sensitive topic handling and a team briefing. You receive the guide as a PDF you can share, and we can add optional extras such as a Canva brand kit or a reply library.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe your voice with examples, not only adjectives like "friendly" or "bold".
- Keep the guide short enough that people will actually open it.
- Include real sentences taken from your best captions.
- Name one person who owns the guide and approves changes.
- Review it when your products, audience or channels change.

**Avoid:**
- Copying another brand's tone because it looks successful.
- Listing so many rules that nobody remembers them.
- Leaving out reply and complaint handling, where tone matters most.
- Treating the guide as final forever, with no updates.
- Sharing it without telling your team why the rules exist.

## Who this is for

This service suits a small business owner who has just hired a freelancer and wants posts to still sound like them. It also suits an online store with a growing team where marketing, support and the founder all post under one name. A brand that is about to hire an agency or an assistant will find that a clear guide shortens the first month.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of your business and customers, your logo and any colors or fonts you already use, and links to your social profiles and website. Add two or three posts you love and any you dislike, with a sentence about why. If you want us to check your live profiles, we only need view access or a public link, and we never need passwords. For anything that needs account access, we work as a collaborator, staff or team user in your own accounts.
